Why this notebook exists

The HT1080 and A549 cell lines were each sequenced once, but the FASTQ files have been re-quantified through two different upstream pipelines at different points in the project. Per-cell-line analyses (2.1.1 A549, 2.2.1 HT1080) all use the NEW counts; older reports (in data/RNAseq/AUG_13_2025_LOY_A549_HT1080/) use the OLD counts. This notebook asks: how comparable are the two count tables, and would the biological conclusions change if we’d kept the OLD counts?

Pipeline difference summary

Field OLD pipeline NEW pipeline
Counts dir data/RNAseq/AUG_13_2025_LOY_A549_HT1080/counts/ projects/RNAseq/counts/AUG_2025_<cell>_LOY/
Aligner HISAT2 STAR two-pass
Reference annotation GENCODE v47 (chr_patch_hapl_scaff) GENCODE v49 (primary assembly)
featureCounts v2.0.1 v2.1.1
Sample composition identical (9 HT1080 + 11 A549) identical

Same biological samples; same FASTQs; different aligner + reference + quantifier version. Differences between the two count tables are therefore technical — they tell us how much downstream interpretation is sensitive to the upstream pipeline choice.

4. Gene-ID harmonization + filtering

The OLD pipeline annotated with GENCODE v47, NEW with v49. Both produce Ensembl IDs like ENSG00000123456.18 (with version suffix). The integer ENSG accession is stable across versions; the suffix changes when the gene’s annotation is updated. We harmonize by stripping the suffix and intersecting on the accession.

## --- HT1080 ----------------------------------------
##   OLD-unique ENSG: 7527
##   NEW-unique ENSG: 24
##   Shared ENSG:     78875
## --- A549 ------------------------------------------
##   OLD-unique ENSG: 7527
##   NEW-unique ENSG: 24
##   Shared ENSG:     78875

7. Sample correlation heatmap (concatenated OLD + NEW)

Concatenate OLD and NEW logCPM matrices for each cell line and cluster all samples together. Same biological sample under two pipelines should cluster together — and if pipeline effects dominate biology, we’d see OLD vs NEW samples cluster by pipeline instead.

## Saved: sample_cor_heatmap_HT1080.(png|pdf)
## Saved: sample_cor_heatmap_A549.(png|pdf)

8. Differential expression on OLD vs NEW: do the conclusions change?

Three contrasts run on each pipeline’s counts:

  1. Paired LOY vs sgCTRL (~ 0 + treatment + passage) — canonical
  2. Unpaired LOY vs sgCTRL (~ 0 + treatment) — passage drift not modeled
  3. Pooled LOY vs (PARENTAL + sgCTRL) — combined Y+ baseline, n=6 vs n=3 (HT1080) or n=7 vs n=4 (A549)

Identical underlying biology under both pipelines → high logFC correlation and substantial DEG overlap regardless of which contrast we pick.

DE concordance: OLD vs NEW pipeline across three contrast types
cell contrast sig_OLD sig_NEW intersect jaccard lfc_r
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 621 579 554 0.8576 0.9908
HT1080 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 65 65 61 0.8841 0.9902
HT1080 LOY vs pooled Y+ 92 84 80 0.8333 0.9912
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (paired) 11 10 10 0.9091 0.9854
A549 LOY vs sgCTRL (unpaired) 9 8 8 0.8889 0.9840
A549 LOY vs pooled Y+ 10 7 7 0.7000 0.9917
